reviews.title: This app is so horrible I had to hesitate to even rate the
Please fix this
reviews.text:
This is a very useful app and could even be a money/life saver if someone gets a hold of your cell phone and has an idea of your passwords (or can get them out of you, somehow). After using it for a couple of months now, I will gladly rate it a 4 1/2 as it is, but it has a potentially dangerous flaw and two programming, nuisances, to wit:

- It should offer the option of disguising the app icon AND NAME to something innocuous, both in picture and name. There is another “App Lock“ offered in the App Store, that allows for this possibility, i.e. changing the app's icon to something like a calculator, for example, but, strangely enough, does not allow the user to change the app's name. Even though the app's icon (and name) can be hidden from view in your cell phone main screen, the app is readily available via a search of your installed apps, where it shows the icon and name (and it even starts with an “A” so…). I installed this app, and use it constantly, because my son (who is a programmer) recommended it to me, and I thought that I had achieved almost total security from this standpoint. However, a few days ago, talking to an Uber driver, regarding the cases in which people have had their bank accounts cleaned out via the app installed in their cell phones, he mentioned to me that I could install an app that would hide, the icons, the conclusion to this being that, if an Uber driver knows about this type of app, undoubtedly crooks would also be aware of these applications and would search for them in the cell phone and, if they also have you, they can beat the pulp out of you until you tell them the PIN and, once they have it, they can deactivate the “Hide“ feature of the app, and then proceeded to get from you the various passwords and PINs needed to transfer money out of your accounts (some of which will even be, no doubt, set up for facial recognition). The app should allow the user to completely disguise it, BOTH THE ICON AND THE NAME, so that it could not be easily found and deactivated, thust increasing security considerably.  Much easier to "explain" that you do not have any financial apps installed "because of the dangers involved...".

Now, for the programming flaws:

- The PIN used to lock/unlock apps is the same used to access the app itself. They should be allowed to be different, i.e. have one “master pin“ to activate/deactivate the various features in the app and other pin(s) to block/unblock block apps.

- Finally, when when one is selecting apps to be blocked, or hidden, the program has a rather disconcerting tendency to return to the main app categories screen when one has already chosen a category and began to choose individual apps to be blocked or hidden, and you have to start all over again.

It would be fantastic if the developers could fix at least the main problem (i.e. disguising the app itself so that it would not provide any clue as to its true identity and purpose)

reviews.title: App Lock is just what I was looking for!!
reviews.text: App Lock works great and was just what I was looking for. Once you learn how to use all the lock features you will really like it. You can also lock your account information and your phone passcode from being changed including the apps of your choice. And the password for App Lock is different from your phone passcode. It locks your apps for a time frame you set. So like if set for 5 minutes it will automatically lock the app you unlocked so you don’t forget to lock the app again. I started receiving an air one morning and emailed support and within a few hours they had to fix update. Great support. Thanks again
